title: Probe-driven throughput throttling sentinel and phased rollback policy
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: We observed noisy throughput regressions during partial rollouts where standard canary detectors were insensitive to short-lived but impactful drops in effective throughput (requests/sec served), causing customer-visible saturation before automatic rollback triggers. This PR introduces a probe-driven throughput sentinel that schedules targeted synthetic probes across cohorts to estimate effective throughput under load, computes a rate-smoothed deviation score, and gates rollouts with a phased rollback policy that escalates from routing throttles to full rollback.

Design summary:
1) Probe scheduler: a new scheduler component (scheduler/probe_scheduler.go) that inserts lightweight synthetic probe requests sampled by traffic slice and time-of-day. Probes capture end-to-end tail and per-step service time for throughput-sensitive routes.
2) Rate-smoothed deviation metric: a quantile-based smoothing window that fuses probe results with production p95/p99 throughput samples to reduce false positives from transient bursts.
3) Phased rollback policy: configurable policy that first reduces new route weight and enables a short hold window (probe re-eval) before triggering a full rollback; each phase has cooldown and manual-override flags.
4) Integration with canary evaluator: new hooks in perf_canary/evaluator.go to consume probe signals and produce a final guard decision object for rollout controller.
5) Telemetry & observability: added metrics (probe.success_rate, probe.throughput_estimate, guard.decision_reason) and a short ops doc for interpreting signals.

Backwards compatibility: All new features are feature-flag gated (env CANARY_PROBE_ENABLED=false by default). No API changes to external customers. Related tickets: ENG-12983 (implementation/design), SUP-452 (customer incident that motivated probe idea).

Implementation highlights and tests:
- Added probe scheduler, probe handler, and controller-facing guard (new files listed below).
- Unit tests for scheduler sampling bounds and deviation scoring.
- Integration test emulating bursty background traffic and targeted probe failures (tests/integration/test_throttle_sentinel.py).
- Local benchmark harness showing <0.8ms median probe overhead on a single vCPU.

Example configs: configs/canary_policy.yaml shows the new phased rollback parameters and probe sampling rates (defaults tuned for 1% sampled probes).

Migration notes: Operators can enable the sentinel gradually per-service via canary policy. Rollout controller supports per-route hold durations.

Request for review: Evaluate correctness of the blended metric, validate cooldowns and phase thresholds, and eyeball telemetry naming.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation of probe scheduler and evaluator hooks
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Docs: ops/throughput-sentinels.md and config examples
- [x] Feature flag gating and defaults

CI: go build & unit tests, python integration tests, linter, and canary-e2e smoke run. Initial CI run had a transient integration test failure (test_throttle_sentinel::ProbeDropScenario) which was a timing race in the synthetic harness; fixed by adding a short jitter in the test harness and re-ran. Merge: squash and merge after approvals.

release_notes:
- Added a probe-driven throughput sentinel that schedules synthetic probes to detect short-lived but impactful throughput regressions.
- Introduced a phased rollback policy that gracefully throttles traffic before full rollback.
- New metrics and ops doc to help SREs interpret sentinel signals.
notes_for_ops: Feature gated behind CANARY_PROBE_ENABLED=false by default. Default probe sample rate is 1% and per-policy smoothing window defaults to 2 minutes. Recommend staging enablement for high-traffic services and gradual ramp to 1%->5% sampling while watching probe.success_rate and guard.decision_reason metrics.
